introduction: This level highlights the structural defects in Timber, the geological classification of building stones, and the crucial physical phenomenon known as the 'Bulking of Sand'.

core_concepts.title: Timber and Seasoning
core_concepts.description:
1. **Seasoning:** The process of drying timber to remove the sap (moisture), which prevents shrinkage and increases strength. 
2. **Moisture Content:** Well-seasoned timber should have a moisture content between 10% to 12%. 
3. **Defects:** Knots (caused by the bases of branches) and Shakes (longitudinal separations in the wood fibers).

core_concepts.title: Building Stones
core_concepts.description:
1. **Geological Classification:** Igneous (e.g., Granite, Basalt), Sedimentary (e.g., Sandstone, Limestone), and Metamorphic (e.g., Marble, Slate). 
2. **Specific Gravity:** A good building stone should have a specific gravity greater than 2.7. 
3. **Crushing Strength:** Should be greater than 100 MPa (or 1000 kg/cm²).

core_concepts.title: Bulking of Sand
core_concepts.description: When 4-5% moisture is added to dry sand, a film of water forms around the sand particles due to **Surface Tension**. This pushes the particles apart, increasing the overall volume of the sand by 20-30%. This phenomenon is called 'Bulking'.

important_entities.name: Plywood
important_entities.significance: Plywood is made by gluing together thin layers of wood (veneers) at right angles (90 degrees) to each other. Because of this cross-lamination, the tensile strength of plywood is equal in all directions (isotropic).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: A frequent question asks for the best stone for DPC (Damp Proof Course) or roofing. Remember, 'Slate' is an excellent roofing material because it can be easily split into thin layers along its natural cleavage planes.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Limestone transforms into Marble. Shale transforms into Slate.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite State AE/JE question: 'What is the primary cause of the bulking of sand?' Answer: Surface Tension.
